rows.name: Sagittarius A*, the black hole at the Milky Way's centre
rows.source: Mass: GRAVITY Collaboration (2023), Astronomy & Astrophysics 677, L10; distance 8,277 pc and position as given on Wikipedia's Sagittarius A* page (CC BY-SA 4.0)

rows.name: The Milky Way, the galaxy as a whole
mass_msun_published: within 200 kpc, as given on Wikipedia
rows.how: Its pull on the Sun, and with it on Earth, is worked out from the Sun's orbit round the centre: speed squared over distance, 220 km/s at 8.32 kpc
rows.source: Wikipedia, Milky Way (CC BY-SA 4.0): masses with their studies; distance 8.32 kpc (Gillessen et al. 2016); speed about 220 km/s

rows.name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
rows.source: Wikipedia, Andromeda Galaxy (CC BY-SA 4.0): mass (1.5 +/- 0.2) x 10^12 solar masses, 765 kpc; the article adds that 2018 radio results give about 8 x 10^11

rows.name: The Great Attractor
rows.source: Wikipedia, Great Attractor (CC BY-SA 4.0): near galactic longitude 307, latitude 9; 150-250 million light-years (NASA 2013); about 10^16 solar masses (Kraan-Korteweg 2005)

rows.name: Laniakea Supercluster, the centre of its pull
rows.source: Tully, Courtois, Hoffman and Pomarede (2014), Nature 513, 71-73; values as given on Wikipedia's Laniakea Supercluster page (CC BY-SA 4.0): centre RA 10h32m, Dec -46 deg, 250 million ly, binding mass 10^17 solar masses
